issues.description: The problem statement requires constructors to accept attributes in the same order as listed in the UML (first attribute on top => first constructor parameter). For ExcellenceLand the UML lists excellencyLevel and excellentEnough as attributes (and the tasks add a rides attribute). However, the solution implements the ExcellenceLand constructor with parameter order (List<Ride> rides, boolean excellentEnough, double excellencyLevel), which does not follow the attribute order implied by the UML/instructions. This mismatch can confuse students about the expected constructor signature and will cause tests that check constructor parameter ordering to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the ExcellenceLand constructor parameter order with the UML/instructions. For example, if the intended attribute order is excellencyLevel, excellentEnough, rides, change the constructor signature to ExcellenceLand(double excellencyLevel, boolean excellentEnough, List<Ride> rides) and assign fields accordingly. Alternatively, clarify the expected attribute order in the problem statement/tests to remove ambiguity.
